candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate accessible services, referrals, continuity, and technology-supported care based on client needs
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telehealth access to diabetes self-management education
candidate.educational_objective: Use telehealth or digital DSMES to reduce access barriers when appropriate while preserving individualized in-person assessment and follow-up when clinically needed.

options.A: Offer telehealth or another appropriate digital DSMES option if it meets the client’s needs and preferences, while maintaining necessary clinical follow-up.
options.B: Discontinue DSMES because education is effective only when delivered face to face.
options.C: Use telehealth as a complete replacement for all in-person medical evaluation regardless of the client’s clinical condition.
options.D: Delay further education until the client can reliably travel to the clinic because remote delivery does not address access barriers.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend offering DSMES through telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction. Telehealth can expand access but does not automatically replace every in-person examination or other clinically necessary care. B and D contradict the guideline’s support for remote DSMES. C overstates telehealth by treating it as a universal substitute for all in-person clinical assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards support telehealth/digital delivery of DSMES to reduce access barriers and meet individual preferences without establishing that remote care universally replaces all in-person clinical evaluation.
candidate.source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: DSMES Recommendation 5.6 — offer DSMES via telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction; person-centered DSMES recommendations 5.1–5.5
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client with diabetes lives far from the clinic and has missed several in-person diabetes self-management education visits because of transportation problems. Which care-planning action is most appropriate?
